items.name: Anushka Jena
items.shortBio: Building the Bhubaneswar pilot so people hear about mediation before court feels like the only door.
items.story:
“Ma’am, you’ll have to come to court every day. Are you sure?”

For many, that question can make pursuing a dispute feel more daunting than walking away. What begins as a fight for what is right can become years of expenses, uncertainty and lost peace. But resolving a dispute shouldn't always mean preparing for a legal battle. Mediation offers another way: a conversation where people can work towards a resolution and retain a say in the outcome. Somewhere in India, someone is about to drop their case. Not because they were wrong. Because fighting costs money, and years of peace. UnLitigate your disputes. Choose your agency.

items.name: Madhur
items.shortBio: Running Pune operations so supervised student mediation has a calm, practical home.
items.story: A dispute should not swallow a whole year of someone's life. Madhur saw how often people wait, then give up, not because the other side was right but because the process was heavier than the problem. Pune is where that observation became operations: a place to try supervised student mediation in a city that moves fast and still gets stuck. The work is practical. Train. Sit down. Write it down. Stay honest about what we can and cannot take. If the other side will not come, we say so. If they will, we make the room calm enough to talk.

items.name: Prakhar
items.shortBio: Carrying the idea to universities, centres and anyone who would otherwise never hear the word mediation.
items.story: Prakhar joined after the project had a name, because the idea was already clear and still needed people who could carry it to universities, centres and anyone who would otherwise never hear the word mediation. Partnerships are how a student initiative becomes something a worried family can trust. The job is to be precise: what is live, what is a pilot, what is still being built. No slogans. Real moments. A first step that does not feel like a fight.
